Maya: quick heads up — Gambit13b (int4) canary in staging started hitting OOMs during long-conversation prompts. seeing memory fragmentation spikes and repeated allocation failures. logs: https://staging-logs.internal/redwood/xyz

Rajesh: noticed that too. pattern looks like KV cache growth + slab churn when sequence + response length > ~2500 tokens. most failures when default max_new_tokens=512.

Maya: repro steps: seed prompt ~1800 tokens + user ask -> model tries to generate ~600 and we hit OOM. dump shows lots of small free/alloc cycles.

Toni: initial theory — aggressive prefetch + large batch windows promote big contiguous allocations that fragment int4 heaps. two quick mitigations: lower max_new_tokens default, shrink batch window.

Maya: agree. propose quick config patch for canary:
```
model_defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  batch_window_ms: 10
  prefetch: false
  kv_eviction_policy: aggressive_trim
  soft_reserve_fraction: 0.06
```

Liz: caution — prefetch=false will slightly increase p95 for some workloads. alternative: keep prefetch but enable `kv_trim_on_alloc` so allocations trigger a light compaction. that tends to help int4 frag.

Rajesh: another idea: dynamic cap based on context length. if context_len > 1024, cap max_new_tokens to 256. pseudocode:
```
if len(context) > 1024:
  max_new_tokens = min(requested, 256)
else:
  max_new_tokens = requested
```
This preserves UX for short prompts but avoids pathological long generations.

Maya: good call. also lower batch_window_ms for high-concurrency routes so we avoid big continuous allocations. combine dynamic cap + kv_trim_on_alloc + soft_reserve tweak.

Infra-bot: deploy queued: canary/gambit13b-int4 env=staging by @Maya at 3551240001 :rocket:

Sam: running a 10k request smoke with mixed prompt lengths now. will report failures and p95.

Sam: smoke finished — 1 OOM in 10k (was ~40 in previous run). frag still present in traces but compactions reduced crash rate. p95 latency +70ms on the canary.

Maya: that reduction is promising. next steps:
- keep dynamic cap in canary rollforward
- add regression unit that simulates long-chain prompts to onboarding tests
- evaluate UX tradeoff (notify devs in changelog)

Liz: please add to the new-model checklist: default_max_new_tokens heuristic, kv_trim_on_alloc recommended for int4, and a note about batch_window tuning.

Maya: opened PR with changes and test: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge/1234

Rajesh: watching the next canary run. if stable, we can roll to dedicated canary with the same defaults. nice job on the triage :thumbsup:
